core.title: Keep high-cardinality identifiers out of metric labels
core.given: A telemetry tracking plan contains a metric item (new, edited or existing).
core.when: You declare or review the metric's dimensions (labels).
core.then: Every dimension declares a cardinality of low or medium; none is declared high and none names a property the item declares cardinality high.
prefer: Keep the identifier, change the signal: label the metric with bounded dimensions (e.g. an outcome, cardinality low) and carry the identifier as an event, log or trace property declared cardinality high — for example on the sibling event's properties. If the identifier is already carried by such a property, removing it from the metric dimensions is enough.

Treat any property whose distinct-value volume is unbounded or near-unbounded (request ids, user ids, session tokens) as a high-cardinality identifier and carry it as an event, log or trace property, where cardinality is the point rather than a liability.
To check a dimension, compare its name with the item's declared properties; if a property of that name is declared cardinality high, the dimension is rejected.
avoid: Dropping the identifier from the plan entirely instead of carrying it as an event/log/trace property.
Leaving a metric dimension's cardinality undeclared, or relabelling a high-cardinality id as low/medium to pass the check.
unless: Event, log and trace properties may declare cardinality high where justified; this rule judges metric dimensions only.
core.why: Every distinct metric-label value becomes a new time series, so a high-cardinality label is a backend outage committed in the plan; the plan is where that mistake is cheapest to catch.
evidence: When the telemetry tracking-plan validator has been run, it reports no finding for the metric item.
Each entry in the metric item's dimensions list has a name and cardinality in {low, medium}.

Each high-cardinality identifier removed from metric dimensions is still carried in the plan as an event, log or trace property (declared cardinality high where justified); a sibling event is one acceptable placement, not a requirement.
verification: Dimension = an entry of the metric item's dimensions list, with a name and a declared cardinality (low, medium or high). High-cardinality identifier = a property whose distinct-value volume is unbounded or near-unbounded (request ids, user ids, session tokens).
Reject a metric item when: a dimension's cardinality is missing; a dimension's cardinality is declared high; or a dimension's name matches a property the item declares cardinality high.

Scope: all metric items regardless of file name or location. A metric item is recognised structurally — by the item's signal kind (metric) and its dimensions list, not by a filename pattern — and the rule applies equally to new, edited and existing items. Event, log and trace properties with cardinality high are legal and not judged.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the enforcement run fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: metric dimension with missing or high cardinality
metric dimension naming a property declared cardinality high

fires: A metric item lists a dimension declared cardinality high.
A metric item lists a dimension with no declared cardinality.
A metric dimension is named after a property (e.g. a request/user/session id) that the item declares cardinality high.
An existing metric item is reviewed or validated and one of its dimensions violates the above, even though nobody is editing it.
doesNotFire: An event, log or trace item declares a property with cardinality high, justified by the plan.
A metric item whose dimensions all declare low or medium cardinality and name no high-cardinality property.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role, so the core can name the artifact class whose metric items this rule judges. The core needs to know that the stack's tracking plan is a plan artifact and what its items are called; recognition of a metric item is structural (signal kind metric plus a dimensions list), never by path or suffix.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is intrinsically stack-neutral: it judges the structure of telemetry tracking-plan metric items (declared dimension cardinality), not any runtime, language or file convention, so the core is nearly verbatim. Neutralizations made: (1) the validator id 'planner_telemetry_plan' (evidence[0], activation.facts[1]) is replaced by 'the telemetry tracking-plan validator' in the core and kept bunOnly; (2) verifier_detail[4]'s concrete fix example with its plan-item path is bunOnly, per the reference-example policy; (3) why's 'with a YAML file attached' flourish is paraphrased away from the Bun plan format; (4) the strict-disposition shared node's 'atdd-bun fails on every finding' is restated as 'the enforcement run fails on every finding'. Recognition of metric items is structural (llm_judged), so no path or suffix profile keys are needed; the only profile input is the concrete plan-artifact kind name via roles.plan_artifact.kinds. Severity 3 / strict disposition stay with the rule in core:verification, not the profile.
